cards.explanation: The answer is the branches of the forest trees, friends. God asks, "…how does the wood of the vine surpass any other branch among the trees in the forest?" (Ezekiel 15:2) It's a setup question, and the answer He's heading toward is that it doesn't. Vine wood is standing in a lineup of tall trees with nothing to brag about.

The answer is a peg to hang utensils on, bakers. God asks, "Or can one make from it a peg on which to hang utensils?" (Ezekiel 15:3) That's about the smallest job you can give a piece of wood. It's just a little hook on the wall. And God is asking whether vine wood can even do that.

The answer is fire, friends. God says, "No, it is cast into the fire for fuel." (Ezekiel 15:4) He asks what the wood could become, and the answer is that it gets burned. Nothing gets built from it. It just goes into the flames.

The answer is True. God says, "Even when it was whole, it could not be made useful." (Ezekiel 15:5) So the fire isn't the reason the wood is no good for building. Whole, it still couldn't make anything useful. Then He adds how much less it can be useful once the fire has charred it.

The answer is Jerusalem, bakers. God says, "Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I will give up the people of Jerusalem." (Ezekiel 15:6) All those questions about wood were building to this. The vine in the picture stands for the people of Jerusalem.

The answer is False, friends. God says, "Though they may have escaped the fire, yet another fire will consume them." (Ezekiel 15:7) So the text doesn't say they're safe from then on. Escaping once doesn't change that, because it says another fire is coming for them.
The answer is that He is the LORD, bakers. God says, "…when I set My face against them, you will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 15:7) What gets known is who He is. That is the point of the verse.

The answer is that the people have acted unfaithfully, friends. God says, "Thus I will make the land desolate, because they have acted unfaithfully…" (Ezekiel 15:8) The text gives the reason right there. It's a heavy one, and I think it's the part of this passage that hurts most.
